title: bzf renovation roadmap
description: A renovation roadmap for one building, `roadmaps/<id>.json`: the steps of a staged renovation in their order, each step's measures and what each measure changes in the building, the target and the assumptions the figures rest on. It is the content of a renovation passport (EPBD Art. 12 and Annex VIII), which in Germany is the individueller Sanierungsfahrplan (iSFP). The building document is the building as it stands and holds no later state. The state after a planned step is the building document with the changes of every planned step up to it applied in order; a done step's changes are in the building document already, and a declined step's are never applied. A writer that marks a step done applies its changes to the building document in the same revision, corrected to what was built. A change of the op `app` changes an app's own documents instead, and a reader that does not know that app cannot derive the states from its step on. Each state's figures (energy, GHG emissions, class, savings, bill savings) are derived by the method that issues the roadmap and are frozen in the issued document (versand.json, type `renovationRoadmap`), never stored here. Costs and funding amounts are commercial and lie apart (costs.json). This schema describes documents of schema version 1.x; a document of another major version is only required to say which.

scheme.description: The scheme it follows: `de:isfp` (Germany's individueller Sanierungsfahrplan), `eu-renovation-passport` (Annex VIII directly), `epc-recommendations` (the recommendations an energy performance certificate gives, EPBD Art. 19(5) to (7): each a step of its own, its savings in the certificate's figures).

visit.description: The on-site visit it rests on (EPBD Art. 12(3)).

heatNetwork.description: Whether a heat network serves or will serve the building, as the municipal heat planning (Wärmeplanung) says (EPBD Annex VIII: district-heating potential).

year.description: When it is expected, where planned.

steps.description: In their order: done steps first, as the building's renovation history, then the planned ones.

target.description: Where the roadmap leads: an energy performance class, a standard (a zero-emission building, an Effizienzhaus level), in words.

class.description: The energy performance class reached after the last step, as the issuing scheme names it: "A", "A+".

standard.description: The standard reached: `zeb` (zero-emission building, EPBD Art. 11), `nzeb`, or a national one with its country (`de:effizienzhaus-55`, `de:effizienzhaus-70`, `de:effizienzhaus-85`, `de:effizienzhaus-denkmal`).

assumptions.description: What the figures rest on beyond the building: energy prices and their increase (EPBD Annex VIII: bill savings with the price assumptions), and the calculation's basis.

prices.description: Energy prices per carrier at the roadmap's date, gross.

perKWh.description: Price per kWh of final energy.

increase.description: Assumed price increase per year, as a fraction.

co2Price.description: Assumed CO₂ price per tonne, where it enters the prices.

method.description: The calculation the figures come from: "DIN V 18599:2018-09" for the iSFP, "DIN/TS 18599:2025-10".

priceSource.description: Where the prices come from: a published price statistic, the owner's bills.

step.description: A step of the roadmap: measures done together, when, and why in this order.

year.description: When it is planned, or when it was done; the first year where it is planned for a range.

until.description: The last year of the range it is planned for.

trigger.description: The occasion it waits for instead of a year: "wenn der Kessel ausgetauscht werden muss".

duration.description: How long it takes to carry out, weeks of seven days (EPBD Annex VIII 2(b)(v)).

status.description: Planned: its changes are still to be made, and a reader applies them to show the building after it. Done: carried out, so its changes are in the building document and are not applied again (EPBD Annex VIII: past major renovations); a renovation from before the building was recorded is a done step without changes. Declined by the owner: kept as advised, never applied. A step whose status a reader doesn't know leaves the states from it on unknown.

rationale.description: Why it comes at this point in the order (EPBD Annex VIII).

measure.description: A measure: what is done to which part of the building, as changes to the building document.

components.description: The component groups it concerns, as a roadmap rates and groups them: roof, top ceiling, external walls, windows, doors, floor or cellar ceiling, heating (generation), hot water, distribution (storage, distribution and emission), ventilation, cooling, lighting, on-site generation, storage, automation. The iSFP rates eight: walls, roof or top ceiling, windows and doors, floor, heating, hot water, distribution, ventilation.

affects.description: The items it concerns: walls, openings, roof plates, systems.

changes.description: What it changes in the building document, or in an app's own documents (op `app`), applied in order. In a planned step they are what is to be done. In a done step they are the record of what was done, as built, and an id in them may be gone from the building (an item the step removed). A measure whose changes include an `app` change says in `affects` and `components` what that change touches, so that a reader that does not know the app still sees which items and component groups the measure concerns.

description.description: What is done, technically, as the owner and the trade read it.

options.description: Technology and material options for it (EPBD Annex VIII).

targets.description: The values the measure promises, as the roadmap states them, so that what is carried out can be checked against it later (the BEG's check that a measure is the iSFP's): a U-value, an insulation's thickness and conductivity, a heat pump's seasonal performance, a PV array's peak power.

quantity.description: What is promised: `uValue` (W/(m²·K)), `thickness` (m), `lambda` (W/(m·K)), `efficiency`, `scop` (a heat pump's Jahresarbeitszahl too), `solarFraction`, `heatRecovery` (fractions), `collectorArea` (m²), `peakPower` (kWp), `storage` (l or kWh), `output` (kW). Any other is kept.

of.description: The item it is promised for, where it isn't all the measure affects.

limit.description: Whether the value is a maximum (a U-value), a minimum (a performance) or exact.

requirements.description: What it requires to be done right: a hydraulic balancing, an airtightness concept, a minimum U-value for funding.

advantages.description: What speaks for it (EPBD Annex VIII 2(b)(i)).

disadvantages.description: What speaks against it (EPBD Annex VIII 2(b)(i)).

funding.description: The funding programmes it may get, by name and link (EPBD Annex VIII: funding sources). The amounts are commercial (costs.json).

change.description: One change: to the building document, a field of an item set (a wall's construction, a system's phase), an item added to a list (a new construction, a new heat pump), or an item removed; items are found by id anywhere in the building, and a field holds what that item's schema allows. Or, since 0.4, a change to an app's own documents (op `app`). Or a newer kind of change.

field.description: The field, as the item's schema names it: "construction", "phase".

into.description: The item whose list it goes into: the building, a part, a storey.

item.description: The item, with an id of its own.

oneOf.description: A change only the named app's own document model knows (since 0.4): what it changes lies in that app's own documents, `Daten/<app>/…`, never in the building document, which only `set`, `add` and `remove` change. A reader that knows the app's document model and has its documents applies it to them, in its place among the changes, to derive the state after the step. Any other reader (one of edition 0.3 or older, which takes it for a newer kind of change, too): MUST keep it as it came, in its place, and write it back unchanged; MUST treat the state after the step that holds it, and every later state and the target, as unknown, deriving no figures for them and showing none as if the change were not there; MAY show the roadmap's own data (steps, measures, `affects`, `components`, `targets`, costs) and the states before that step. A done step's `app` changes are in the app's documents already and a declined step's are never applied, so neither leaves a state unknown. A writer that marks a step done applies its `app` changes to the app's documents in the same revision as the rest; a writer that does not know the app does not mark such a step done.

app.description: The app, by the name of its own folder under `Daten/` (`energieberatung` for `Daten/energieberatung/…`, whose class the project root's `classes` gives under `energieberatung/`): one path segment, not starting with a dot, and none of the folders this specification defines.

change.description: The change as the app's own document model describes it: opaque to every other reader. It follows the format's writing rules (README, "How the documents are written"): keys in English, free text in the project's language, items of the project named by their ids.

oneOf.description: A newer kind of change, kept as it came; a reader that doesn't know it shows the step's state after it as unknown.
